design.text: Multicenter, randomized, active-controlled noninferiority trial comparing treosulfan to busulfan, each in combination with fludarabine, as a preparative regimen for allogeneic HSCT; noninferiority margin of 1.3 on the hazard ratio scale, with superiority testing if noninferiority demonstrated.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) within 2 years after transplantation (events: disease relapse, graft failure, or death).

result.text: Positive on primary endpoint EFS (noninferiority p = 0.0000164 vs efficacy boundary 0.000149); FDA-adjudicated EFS HR 0.65 (95% CI: 0.50, 0.85) in ITT. FDA relied on OS: HR 0.67 (95% CI: 0.51, 0.90) in ITT (no p-value, no prespecified alpha for OS).

citations.quote: Study MC FludT.14/L Trial II was considered a positive study based on the primary endpoint of EFS (non-inferiority p-value = 0.0000164 as compared to an efficacy boundary of 0.000149). Based on FDA-adjudication of EFS events, the hazard ratio for EFS was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.50, 0.85) in the ITT population.
The HR for OS (Cox proportional hazards model, stratified by donor type and risk group) compared to busulfan was 0.67 (95% CI: 0.51, 0.90) in the ITT population

indication.text: In combination with fludarabine as a preparative regimen for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in adult and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) or with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS).
